title: The Spire of Ironhollow
premise: Silas Fairweather survives in the magic-outlawed city of Ironhollow by stealing memories and bottling them as harmless charms. When a dying courier forces a map into his hands — a map to the Spire, where the last true magic sleeps — Silas becomes the hunted bearer of a secret that could reignite the war that made magic illegal. Pursued by the Wardens and the memory-eating thing they serve, he gathers a crew of outcasts and follows the map through the drowned undercity to the Spire itself. There he learns the map's true purpose: the dying stranger chose him not at random, but because a stolen memory Silas sold years ago belonged to her. In the end Silas must give up his own most precious memory — the face of his dead sister — to unbind the Spire's power and shatter the Wardens' master, choosing to let magic return to the world at the cost of never knowing why he fought for it.
about_author: E. M. Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a northern port city before turning to fiction. They write about thieves, debts, and the things people bury to survive.

chapters.title: The Taste of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: POV Silas. In Ironhollow's night market, Silas steals a memory of the sea from a grieving sailor and bottles it as a charm. The chapter establishes his trade, his guilt, and the city's fear of magic. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Blood on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: POV Silas. A stranger collapses in Silas's stairwell, bleeding from a wound that won't close, and presses a folded map into his hands with a warning: 'She'll know you have it.' Wardens arrive; Silas flees through the rooftops. Emotional beat: terror and the first crack in his careful, small life.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Take
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Hiding in a memory-den, Silas watches Wardens drain a den-full of people into grey-eyed husks. He glimpses the thing beneath the Warden commander's skin. Emotional beat: dawning horror — this is what waits for anyone caught with magic.

chapters.title: The Debtor's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas seeks out Brannock, a fence who owes him, to decode the map's water-stained script. Brannock names the Spire and refuses to help — then is taken that night. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt; Silas realizes helping him is already fatal.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Sold the Sea
chapters.summary: POV Silas. A young thief, Wren, blackmails her way into his crew, claiming she saw the stranger's killer. Silas recognizes her as the girl who bought his sister's memory years ago. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance, buried grief stirred.

chapters.title: Down Among the Drowned Streets
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren leads Silas into the flooded undercity toward the map's first marker. They evade Warden patrols and find the stranger's hidden cache: letters proving the outlawing of magic was built on a lie. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into anger at the city's founding myth.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The letters lead to Odile, the dying stranger's daughter, a disgraced Warden archivist. She confirms the map is real and reveals her mother died carrying it. Silas suspects she wants it for herself. Emotional beat: distrust sharpening into reluctant respect.

chapters.title: A Charm of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas sells a memory to pay for passage and finds the buyer is a Warden informant. He barely escapes, but the Wardens now know his face and trade. Emotional beat: the price of survival — every deal costs more than coin.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Toll
chapters.summary: POV Wren. To cross the Sunken Gate, the crew must pay the ferryman in memories. Wren gives up her memory of her mother's lullaby without hesitation; Silas refuses to pay at all and bargains instead. Emotional beat: contrast between Wren's grief-hardened sacrifice and Silas's hoarding.

chapters.title: What Brannock Knew
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Odile finds Brannock husked but alive, and reads the residue of his drained memories: the Wardens' master, the Hollow King, was the first mage to outlaw magic — to keep it all for himself. Emotional beat: revelation and cold resolve.

chapters.title: The Spire on the Map
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The map's final leg reveals the Spire lies beneath Ironhollow itself, under the Warden citadel. The crew realizes they've been walking toward the enemy's heart. Emotional beat: dread; the trap and the destination are the same place.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Fairweather House
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The Wardens burn Silas's old tenement and everyone who ever bought a charm from him. Wren is captured covering the crew's escape. Emotional beat: rage and self-loathing — his trade made all of them targets.

chapters.title: The Grey-Eyed Prisoner
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Odile goes into the citadel alone, using her Warden credentials, and finds Wren half-drained but fighting. She frees her, learning Wren has carried a fragment of the stranger's memory since childhood. Emotional beat: fierce, unexpected tenderness.

chapters.title: Bargain with the Hollow King
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Captured, Silas is brought before the Hollow King, who offers him his sister's memory back — and immortality — if he surrenders the map. Silas, starving for the past, nearly accepts. Emotional beat: temptation at its most intimate.

chapters.title: The Memory He Sold
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren reveals the truth: the memory Silas stole and sold years ago was the dying stranger's — a memory of the Spire's unbinding rite. The stranger chose him deliberately. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as inheritance; Silas was chosen, not cursed.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: POV Silas. In a smuggler's cellar, Odile and Wren reconstruct the rite from the letters and Wren's fragment. It requires a freely given memory of absolute love. Silas understands what it will cost. Emotional beat: quiet, terrible acceptance.

chapters.title: Storming the Undercroft
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The crew descends into the Spire through the citadel's drowned foundations as alarms rise. Odile holds a corridor alone; Brannock, half-husked, dies buying them seconds. Emotional beat: camaraderie forged in sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Heart of Ironhollow
chapters.summary: POV Silas. At the Spire's heart, Silas confronts the Hollow King, who reveals the war never ended — he simply imprisoned it. Magic isn't a weapon here; it's a prisoner. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — power hoarded is power rotted.

chapters.title: The Face He Gave Away
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas speaks his sister's memory aloud — her laugh, her face, her name — and lets it go into the rite. The Spire opens. Emotional beat: the climax of grief and love; he unbinds magic and loses the reason he had for anything.

chapters.title: The King Unmade
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Freed magic floods the undercity and unmakes the Hollow King, whose power was only the stolen hoard. Odile chooses to remember him as a warning, not a monster, and records the truth. Emotional beat: catharsis and the burden of witness.

chapters.title: A City That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Ironhollow wakes with magic in its gutters and its people remembering what was taken. Wren, restored in part by the Spire's overflow, refuses to lead — she'd rather walk beside Silas. Emotional beat: hope without erasure of cost.

chapters.title: The Charm with No Name
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas, unable to remember why he fought, finds in his pocket a charm he apparently made: inside it, a memory of a girl laughing. He chooses not to open it — some inheritances are carried, not spent. Emotional beat: bittersweet, open-hearted close.
